newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cathay mulls HK-Auckland daily flights.
newsitem.headline: Cathay mulls HK-Auckland daily flights.

text.p: Hong Kong flag carrier Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd said on Friday it is tentatively planning to run daily flights between Hong Kong and Auckland from 1998, probably after Hong Kong's new Chek Lap Kok airport opens.

The airline, which operates five Hong Kong-Auckland flights a week at present, is allowed to step up the service to a daily basis under new air traffic arrangements between Hong Kong and New Zealand, spokeswoman Edna Lam said by telephone.
But she stressed that was a tentative plan and the company was still studying how best to use the additional capacity, and a final decision would not made for some months at least.

Hong Kong and New Zealand recently concluded new air traffic arrangements that provide for a balanced exchange of traffic rights for the airlines of both territories, the Hong Kong government said on Friday.

The arrangements provide the airlines in Hong Kong and New Zealand with new fifth freedom points in Australia, offering travellers the ability to stop over there on their trips from Hong Kong to New Zealand, and vice versa, a spokesman for the Economic Services Branch said in a statement.
The arrangements were concluded in talks between the two sides in Wellington, New Zealand, on February 20 and 21, but have only just been brought into effect, the statement said.

A total 32,900 Hong Kong residents visited New Zealand in 1996, an increase of about 12 per cent over 1995. About 58,000 New Zealand residents visited the territory last year, up 16 per cent over 1995, the government said.
